body.text: Which Turkish marinas (Yalıkavak, D-Marin Göcek, Port Göcek, Setur Kaş) serve superyachts?

Four main hubs anchor superyacht cruising along Türkiye's southwest coast: [Yalıkavak Marina](https://yalikavakmarina.com.tr/marina/about-us/) for vessels up to 140m LOA, [D-Marin Göcek](https://www.d-marin.com/en/news/gold-anchors-for-all-of-d-marins-turkish-marinas/) for sheltered bays up to 70–85m, [Setur Göcek Village Port](https://www.seturmarinas.com/en/marinas/gocek-village-port) for heavy haul-out and charter logistics, and [Setur Marinas](https://www.seturmarinas.com/en) at Kaş for Kekova and Lycian cruising.

Yalıkavak Marina on the Bodrum Peninsula holds a TYHA 5 Gold Anchors rating, 620 berths, an on-site helipad, duty-free fuel access, and Port of Entry status—making it the natural base for 50m+ motor yachts. Further southeast, the Gulf of Fethiye offers flat, pine-sheltered water just 20 minutes from Dalaman International Airport: [D-Marin's Türkiye network](https://www.d-marin.com/en/blog/top-20-marinas-in-turkiye/) operates 380+ berths at D-Marin Göcek and 550 berths at D-Marin Turgutreis, while Setur Göcek Village Port adds a 36,000 m² boatyard with 200-ton and 75-ton travel lifts. Eastward, Setur Kaş Marina provides modern stern-to berths and easy access to the protected Kekova Roads.

body.text: How do transit-log formalities and Greek-island clearances work?

Under [Ministry of Culture and Tourism rules for foreign-flagged yachts](https://www.ktb.gov.tr/EN-99341/entry-and-exit-of-foreign-flagged-yachts.html), every yacht entering or departing Turkish waters must clear customs, passport police, and the harbour master at an official frontier port and carry a valid Transit Log (Yat Kayıt Belgesi).

If your charter combines Bodrum or Göcek with nearby Dodecanese islands such as Kos, Symi, or Rhodes, your captain or yacht agent must formally check out of a Turkish Port of Entry (typically Bodrum, Yalıkavak, Marmaris, Fethiye, or Kaş) and check in at the designated Greek port before cruising Greek waters. As [Viago Yachting's cross-border clearance guide](https://www.viagoyachting.com/en/blog/crossing-to-the-greek-islands-with-a-charter-boat-transit-log-documents-and-routes) notes, returning to Türkiye requires a fresh entry stamp and updated transit-log registration. Allow one to two hours per border formalities stop and verify Schengen visa eligibility for every guest and crew member well before departure.
What provisioning and onshore concierge services can be arranged?

Superyacht provisioning along the Bodrum–Göcek corridor covers organic Aegean produce, local day-boat seafood, specialty imported wines, floral arrangements, and crew logistics delivered directly to the quay. Onshore concierge coordination pairs yacht arrivals with private airport tarmac-to-pier transfers, helicopter hops, restaurant jetties, and licensed archaeological guides for inland ruins.

Rather than relying on default marina brokers who add percentage surcharges to shore excursions and restaurant bookings, yacht owners and charter guests often separate maritime agency work from onshore travel planning. That keeps inland visits—such as private morning tours of Ephesus, Knidos, or Kaunos—aligned cleanly with tender drop-off times and afternoon meltemi wind patterns.
When do marina berths book out for July–August?

Prime 40m+ superyacht berths at Yalıkavak Marina and D-Marin Göcek for July and August frequently sell out between January and March. For June or September—when sea temperatures stay warm and anchorages are quieter—reserve berths at least eight to twelve weeks in advance.
Before locking in your summer cruising schedule, confirm these operational items:

items: Verify vessel LOA, beam, draft, and three-phase shore-power amperage requirements with the marina office.
Confirm whether your itinerary crosses into Greece so transit-log fees and port-of-entry timings are budgeted upfront.
Book Dalaman or Milas–Bodrum VIP airport transfers and any inland guides alongside your berth confirmation.
Check local no-anchoring zones in archaeologically protected bays such as Kekova Roads.

faq.q: Which Turkish marina handles the largest superyachts?
faq.a: Yalıkavak Marina on the Bodrum Peninsula accommodates superyachts up to 140m LOA with 620 berths, three-phase shore power, duty-free fuel, a helipad, and Port of Entry clearance.

faq.q: Is Göcek better than Bodrum for quiet family sailing?
faq.a: Yes. The Gulf of Fethiye around Göcek offers sheltered, flat water and short 20-to-45-minute hops between pine-fringed coves, with Dalaman International Airport only 20 minutes from the marinas.

faq.q: Can we sail directly from a Turkish cove to a Greek island without stopping at a port?
faq.a: No. Both Türkiye and Greece require yachts to check out and check in at official Ports of Entry with passports, crew lists, and transit-log paperwork before visiting anchorages across the maritime border.

faq.q: What is Türkiye's Blue Card (Mavi Kart) system for yachts?
faq.a: Türkiye enforces strict marine-environment rules along the Muğla and Antalya coasts requiring vessels to log black- and grey-water pump-outs digitally at authorised marina stations.

faq.q: When is the best weather window for private sailing in Türkiye?
faq.a: Late May to June and September to mid-October deliver warm swimming water, lighter crowds, and more comfortable daytime temperatures than the peak heat of late July and August.

faq.q: Does Itinerary of Türkiye take commissions from yacht brokers or marinas?
faq.a: No. We are paid exclusively by our clients via a flat planning fee, so our onshore and coastal recommendations remain independent of broker or marina kickbacks.
